description: Parameters of the relief layer of the fictional world (layer 4, experiment E01). Elevations in metres relative to this world's sea level.

plain_noise._source: half the plain amplitudes of the first world's relief layer (shields 450 +- 250 m, platforms 250 +- 120 m, basins 100 +- 50 m, plateaus 1500 +- 300 m)

ridges._note: ridge-and-valley amplitude (std) as a share of the cell's elevation above sea level; plateaus are smooth on top (Tibet), young belts and arcs rough
ridges._strike_note: ridges and valleys run along the strike of a belt, typically 3-5 times longer than wide (fold-and-thrust belts: Appalachians, Zagros, Jura): plane waves weighted by |cos|^12 of the angle to the across-strike direction (the gradient of crustal thickness smoothed over ~50 km); full anisotropy where the thickness changes by 20 m per km or more (belt flanks), isotropic on plateau tops and plains

margin._source: first world E08: a shelf to ~130 m over the inner 40 % of the margin, then a slope to the ocean floor; Earth's shelf break lies at ~130-140 m

ocean._sediment_source: first world E08 run p, fitted to GlobSed (Straume et al. 2019): margins 3044 m, far ocean 404 m, 337 M km3; isostatic rise (3300 - 2000)/(3300 - 1030)
ocean._residual_source: first world E08: residual depth rms 261 m (Earth: +-1 km at ~1000 km); abyssal hills +-150 m

hotspot._source: Hawaiian chain summits: Mauna Kea 4207 m (0-1 Ma), Haleakala 3055 m (~1.3 Ma), Kaala 1220 m (Oahu ~3 Ma), Kawaikini 1598 m (Kauai ~5 Ma), Nihoa 272 m (~7 Ma), Necker 84 m (~10 Ma), French Frigate Shoals at sea level (~12 Ma); fitted by 4200 - 1300 sqrt(age). Below sea level the subsidence slows and the edifice keeps standing ~3 km above the floor (Emperor seamounts, -1 to -3 km). Secondary hotspots: Teide 3715 m, Fogo 2829 m, Pico 2351 m. Big Island ~130 km across.

arc._source: island-arc volcanoes: Lesser Antilles ~1.2-1.5 km, Aleutians up to ~2.8 km; continental arcs: stratovolcanoes stand ~1-2.5 km above the mean of the surrounding arc (Andes, Cascades; the arc cell mean already holds part of the relief)

subgrid._note: expected peak-to-valley relief inside a 10 km cell; the first world used 40 m + 0.9 x range height above the plain and 300 m on the sea floor
